title: Prove the sharp codimension bound for partial query acquisition
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with exact finite corroboration: pruning any cheapest full-span query basis to a dimension-d target space in a rank-r query pool has the sharp acquisition approximation factor r-d+1. The theorem holds over every field with nonnegative costs. A binary family approaches the factor with positive integer costs and a unique cheapest full-span basis.

```text
B = any minimum-cost basis of the entire query span
C = union of B-coordinate supports of the target subspace
cost(C) <= (r-d+1) OPT(target)
```

The new step uses target dimension in a price-threshold argument and supplies a matching family. Ali Romman #5791 supplies the partial-target question and whole-span acquisition contract; the cheap-prefix property and weighted basis exchange are classical. No predecessor implementation or result is audited or replayed. No literature-wide priority for approximation theory is claimed.

## Evidence

Before, whole-span optimality supplied no stated partial-target guarantee. After, the written proof gives the sharp codimension factor, including all tied minimum bases and zero costs.

Local CPython 3.12.15 checks pass at `79965dcf726c077859afe8901eb8e32a236e642f`:

- 123,481 minimum-basis/target comparisons across 256 weighted pools and all 67 subspaces of F2^4, with exhaustive partial-acquisition optima.
- 243,947 pointwise price-threshold checks, 30 unique-basis sharp fixtures, three hypothesis controls and four malformed-input rejections.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized direct replays, both registered commands, package metadata, committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export integrity and a separate optimized replay of the Git-free export.
- `PASS_PARTIAL_QUERY_BASIS_GAP`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` and `PASS_RESEARCH_EXPORT`. The two registered checks took 1.64 seconds together; direct normal and optimized checks took 0.63 and 0.61 seconds. Generated receipts bound all five package files; temporary receipts and research scratch are removed after publication.

From the worktree root, reproduce with:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/partial-query-basis-gap
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/partial-query-basis-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/partial-query-basis-gap/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/partial-query-basis-gap --check-source-history
```

## Limitations

Each acquired query is paid once; linear reconstruction is free only in this declared relaxation. Physical delivery, XOR/scalar reconstruction, restoration, owned storage, native legality and supplier admission require separate costs and proofs. Binary finite checks corroborate the all-field written argument. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No Lean, Docker, selected cold replay, rounded caller or complete multiplication theorem was run. The selected frontier and its five framework assumptions are unchanged.

The formal-interface card is explicitly changed to this algebraic side result. The advance [CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19214980), exact source citation, scope and overlap limits are recorded in the package. Refreshed canonical main remains `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`.

## Open next questions

- Can target-aware acquisition improve the r-d+1 factor with a small checkable certificate? A full-span basis tie rule cannot remove this obstruction, since the sharp family has a unique minimum basis.
- Which actual source caller satisfies the additive acquisition model after reconstruction, delivery, restoration and storage are priced?

## Related open work

- #5791 optimizes whole-span binary query acquisition and explicitly leaves partial-span targets separate. This contribution proves the sharp partial-target loss bound for pruning any of its valid whole-span optima, without depending on its pending code.

Related open work was refreshed after CI against this account's open PRs created since the advance CLAIM. No additional PR on the same partial-target acquisition quantity was found.

## CI notes

At commit `79965dcf726c077859afe8901eb8e32a236e642f`, the [registered-package run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40491092470) failed in `plan`, solely at [Onboarding helper tests](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40491092470/job/122144919721). All ten failure/error entries are in unchanged `tests/test_research_current_assignment.py`; the log ends `FAILED (failures=8, errors=2, skipped=22)`. The two errors are `KeyError: 'follow_up_steps'` and `KeyError: 'catalog_first_step'`. This is the shared onboarding failure on base `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, outside this package. The ten failure/error labels and final failure summary match [PR #5879's failed run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40491123999/job/122145027998) exactly; both logs were inspected.

The [package replay was skipped](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40491092470/job/122147500245). **Hosted replay has not certified this package; only local verification has run.** The local checks listed above passed. The shared failure is left for maintainers; no shared file or onboarding test was changed.

**Blast Radius:** research. No shared implementation, frozen predecessor or selected-result change.
